messages:
samir: Posting results from the quick usability spike on the burst chip. TL;DR: lots of people miss it unless we surface it differently. Link to recording in Figma comments.

jodie: I noticed that in the prototype users thought the tiny burst dot was decorative. Two suggestions: 1) add a visible label (e.g., 'burst') next to the number, or 2) keep dot but make it interactive with a clear affordance. Which do we prefer?

felix: From an implementation POV the interactive chip is easy. We can make it keyboard-focusable and expose aria-labels. But we should validate which copy performs better. Recommend an A/B test: variant A = 'Burst cushion', variant B = 'Temporary capacity'. Track clicks/expansions and whether users read the popover.

terry: Love the AB idea. Also suggest we instrument a tiny funnel: event: autoscale.burst_shown, autoscale.burst_focused, autoscale.burst_expanded, autoscale.burst_apply. We can run for two weeks. If expansion rate < 12% we need a stronger visual.

morgan: Quick research note: when we used 'cushion' previously, some users thought it was financial (cushion = buffer in billing). 'Temporary capacity' tested clearer in moderated sessions. Maybe test three variants? 'Burst', 'Burst cushion', 'Temporary capacity'. But keep the test manageable (2 vs 3).

samir: Good points. Let's do 3-arm test but smaller sample. Metric: expand rate and secondary: time-to-action to change max. Also capture qualitative clicks on the policy link inside popover.

jodie: Design tweak: make the chip include a small affordance caret so users know it expands. Also increase hit target to 44px. On collapsed state the chip shows: 'burst • +3' where +3 is the available headroom. On expanded state show short bullets: 'Adds up to 3 GPUs for short spikes', 'May increase hourly cost ~20%', 'Quota/region limitations'.

felix: Accessibility: chip needs aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-expanded and an aria-label that contains both state and count: e.g., aria-label="Burst available, adds up to 3 GPUs; press Enter for details". When expanded the popover should have role=dialog and an h1/h2 inside that screen readers get.

access-bot: a11y-check: include aria-live="polite" updates when the user applies burst, and ensure keyboard users can close popover with Escape. Also ensure color contrast of chip text >=4.5:1.

terry: On telemetry, please also record variant id (burst_label_variant) and UI density (compact vs spacious) so we can segment by screen size. We'll check correlation with expansion.

morgan: Small copy experiment: inside the popover show a short CTA-style sentence: 'Try burst for short spikes — undo anytime'. We can A/B that against more formal 'Burst provides temporary extra capacity; additional charges may apply.' See what drives adoption without surprising users.

samir: Decision checklist: 1) implement interactive burst chip with caret and 44px hit target, 2) add aria attributes per Felix + Access-bot notes, 3) run 3-arm AB test ("Burst", "Burst cushion", "Temporary capacity") instrumenting autoscale.burst_* events and variant id, 4) show small headroom number inline, 5) popover content will include clear cost delta and policy link, 6) if expansion <12% after 2 weeks increase visual prominence.

jodie: I'll update Figma with three label variants and the caret + expanded content. Felix can add aria examples in the handoff doc. Terry will own telemetry. Morgan will write microcopy options for the popover CTA.

felix: Quick aria snippet for spec: `<button aria-haspopup=\"dialog\" aria-expanded=\"false\" aria-label=\"Burst available, adds up to 3 GPUs; press Enter for details\">burst • +3 ▾</button>`

access-bot: Logged task AUTOSCALE-1144: "Burst discovery A/B test + a11y + instrumentation" assigned to jodie, felix, terry, morgan.

samir: Thanks team — punt back if anyone expects conflict with other rollout naming. Otherwise we'll spin the experiment and reconvene after initial telemetry.
